Rules / Maintainability

SK7090 A thrown NotImplementedException has no issue reference

A member's body is throw new NotImplementedException() and nothing names the issue that owes the implementation.

CategoryMaintainability
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since1.3
SupersedesS3717

Why

⚠ This is SK7040's requirement on the form that compiles, and it sits on Skala's premise rather than beside it. A model asked for an implementation produces a signature with a throw new NotImplementedException() body far more readily than it says it cannot do the work — and that body type-checks, binds, formats, and passes every analyzer in the build. It fails only when it runs, in a caller that had no way to know. A TODO at least announces itself to whoever opens the line; this announces itself to nobody. The requirement is therefore the same one SK7040 makes: somewhere a reader will already be looking, name the issue that owns finishing this. The same vocabulary is accepted — a URL, #123, or a project key such as SKALA-123 — read from the exception's own message, from the throw's own comments, or from the enclosing member's leading trivia.

Example

Instead of:

public decimal Total(Order order) => throw new NotImplementedException();

Write:

// TODO SKALA-412: the discount table is not specified yet.
public decimal Total(Order order) => throw new NotImplementedException("SKALA-412");

When it does not fire

⚠ Report-only, and deliberately so: no edit writes the implementation, and every mechanical guess available — delete the member, return default, change the exception type — turns a loud failure into a quiet one, which is strictly worse than what is there. Only a construction that is thrown is reported; Sonar's S3717 tracks every use of the type, but constructing one to compare against or to hand to a test helper is not a member that compiles and does not work. ⚠ `NotSupportedException` and `UnreachableException` never fire, and that is the rule's position rather than an omission. Both are permanent statements about a contract — an operation this type will never offer, a branch the author asserts is unreachable — and they are what an author writes when the answer really is "not here". NotImplementedException is the one that means "not yet", and "not yet" is what needs an owner. A repository that uses source comments as its backlog should disable the rule, exactly as it would SK7040. ⚠ Test doubles are the one class measured to fire in volume, and the rule does not exempt them. Wrapped in a project file, three slices of Testing/corpus/real/newtonsoft produce nine findings, every one of them a member of a fake implementing an interface the test never calls; the corpus holds twelve such throws and not one carries a reference. The rule's position is that a fake noting that nothing calls the member is exactly the sentence the finding asks for, and a repository that disagrees should path-scope the severity to its test projects. Generated code is excluded.

Configuration

  • dotnet_diagnostic.SK7090.severity
